correctness.rationale: Surjective 15-bit reduction of the additive Fourier transform is algebraically proved, preserving 2^21 fibers. Two different exact-arithmetic algorithms agree on all 32768 signed matching sums, whose 19-level histogram yields 6825 zeros, 25943 nonzeros, least nonzero magnitude four. Exhaustive relabeling of all 6825 zeros gives 26 orbits and sharp 5-edge support classes. Exact integer Fourier transform of the nonzero-mask computes kernel mass 1524338/32768=762169/16384. Both check Parseval. The finding is finite and completely exhausted, without an infinite extrapolation.

value.rationale: After the zero-free orders four and five, the six-label convolution returns to a nontrivial Fourier nullspace, giving a natural exact benchmark. Its full signed 19-level spectrum is an exact inverse-problem benchmark, the two graph types attaining the minimum cancelling support give a sharp structural boundary, and the exact projection endpoint constant quantifies noise amplification beyond spectral inverse-on-range norm. This is a motivated complete finite classification rather than an arbitrary subgraph parameter or mere counting of involutions.
